content: Marrubium vulgare, commonly known as White Horehound or Common Horehound, is a flowering plant that belongs to the Lamiaceae family. It is native to regions of Europe, northern Africa, and Asia. This plant is a herbaceous perennial with greyish leaves and bears a resemblance to mint in its overall appearance. It typically grows to a height of 25 to 45 centimeters. The leaves of Marrubium vulgare measure approximately 2 to 5 centimeters in length and are characterized by a densely crinkled surface. They are also covered with fine, downy hairs. The flowers of this plant are white in color and are arranged in clusters located on the upper portion of the main stem. Like other members of the Lamiaceae family, White Horehound features a distinctive square-shaped stem. Historically, White Horehound has been utilized in the production of cough remedies and hard candies due to its medicinal properties. Additionally, Marrubium vulgare has found application in agriculture as a natural repellent for grasshoppers.
